reasoning.content: Open “Find directions between two points,” enter the “From” and “To” locations, select the requested travel mode in the route-profile combobox, and click “Go”; verify both fields resolve to full canonical locations so similarly named places are not confused. Once the “Directions” report appears, return the visible resolved endpoints, selected mode, complete distance and estimated time, plus the key turn-by-turn roads, ramps, highways, exits, and final approach—never replace the displayed result with a bare completion message or guessed details.

reasoning.title: Verify resolution, then report the visible route
reasoning.description: Use this for requests to calculate directions on the map; it does not apply when the user only asks to locate or display a single place.
reasoning.content: Open “Find directions between two points,” fill the “From” and “To” fields, select the requested mode in the travel-mode combobox, and press “Go”; verify both fields change to the intended canonical place labels, since unchanged query text can look like a resolved endpoint and near-identical venues may differ. Once the “Directions” panel appears, read and report the full visible endpoint labels, distance, time, and all requested or key instruction rows—including road names, exits, and maneuvers—rather than merely confirming completion; rerun with a more precise place query if either endpoint or the route details are not visibly resolved.

reasoning.title: Verify endpoints, then report the complete Directions result
reasoning.description: Use this whenever a route is requested; if the user asks only to configure or display a route, confirmation may suffice, but directions requests require extracting the visible result.
reasoning.content: Open “Find directions between two points,” enter the “From” and “To” locations, verify both fields resolve to the intended canonical places rather than similarly named variants, confirm the requested travel mode in the combobox, and select “Go.” In the resulting “Directions” panel, report the resolved endpoints, selected mode, full displayed distance and time, and every visible turn-by-turn row with its segment distance when detailed directions are requested—never replace the retrieved result with a generic completion message or infer details not shown.

reasoning.title: Verify exact endpoints and extract the complete itinerary
reasoning.description: Apply whenever a directions request names a specific venue or other place that may have near-identical search matches; simple coordinate-to-coordinate requests with already verified markers need no name disambiguation.
reasoning.content: Open “Find directions between two points,” enter both endpoints, select the requested travel mode, and use “Go”; accept the route only after both textboxes display canonical labels whose full names and locations match the request—do not substitute a similarly named place merely because it resolves. In the visible “Directions” panel, report the displayed distance and time plus every numbered instruction and segment distance in the table, rather than returning only the summary or guessing from the map.

reasoning.title: Verify the route, then extract the visible directions
reasoning.description: Use whenever a task asks for directions on the map site; a plotted line or successful “Go” action alone is not a complete result.
reasoning.content: Open “Find directions between two points,” fill “From” and “To,” select the requested travel mode, click “Go,” and verify both fields resolve to the intended canonical places and localities—especially when near-identical venue names exist. In the visible “Directions” panel, copy the complete distance and time and report the turn-by-turn table (every maneuver when full directions are requested, otherwise at least the major roads, exits, and final approach); never replace these visible results with a generic completion message or guessed route.

reasoning.title: Verify exact endpoints before routing
reasoning.description: Apply when a From or To entry remains unresolved, is ambiguous, or has a near-identical place-name match; not when the displayed canonical label and address already confirm the requested place.
reasoning.content: In the directions panel, use search results or a verified address to select the exact requested endpoint—inspect every plausible matching candidate and do not silently substitute a similarly named venue—then confirm both fields show full canonical labels, select the requested travel mode in the mode combobox, and click “Go.” Accept and report the route only when the “Directions” section is visibly displayed for those exact endpoints, copying its complete distance and time values rather than inferring them from the map or an unresolved text entry.

reasoning.title: Verify exact endpoints before reporting the complete route
reasoning.description: Apply whenever a directions endpoint remains raw text, fails to resolve, or resolves to a similarly named place; this is unnecessary only when both displayed canonical place names and locations clearly match the request.
reasoning.content: Open “Find directions between two points,” resolve each POI through the site’s search results or place detail view, confirm its full name and locality, select the requested travel mode, and click “Go”; do not silently replace an unresolved POI with a look-alike. In the “Directions” panel, verify the canonical “From” and “To” values remain correct, then report the full visible distance and time plus every displayed maneuver and segment distance requested—not merely the summary or guessed details.

reasoning.title: Resolve exact endpoints and return the visible route
reasoning.description: Use for map direction tasks, especially when a query is unresolved or has similarly named POIs; do not accept a nearby look-alike or use this workflow for simple place lookup without routing.
reasoning.content: Open “Find directions between two points,” select each endpoint from search results or its detail view, verify the full canonical name and locality in the “From” and “To” fields, choose the requested travel mode, and select “Go.” In the resulting “Directions” panel, report the resolved endpoints, complete displayed distance and duration, and all requested maneuvers and segment distances—or at least the major roads, exits, and final approach—rather than replying with a completion message, a summary alone, or guessed details.

reasoning.title: Search, verify candidates, then route on foot
reasoning.description: Use when a task asks for the nearest place meeting ownership/category constraints and a walking route; do not use this workflow when only a single location lookup is requested.
reasoning.content: Enter the origin in the visible “Search” textbox and select the correct full-address result, search for nearby category candidates, then open each place’s detail view to verify its complete name, chain identity, and local ownership rather than inferring from a similar name or map position; include every tied qualifying candidate. Select “Find directions between two points,” set the verified origin and destination, choose the walking profile, and report the complete visible route steps and distance, confirming the chosen destination has the shortest displayed walking route rather than merely appearing closest in a straight line.

reasoning.title: Localize, qualify, compare, then route
reasoning.description: Use when a task asks for the closest place meeting category or ownership criteria and requests walking directions; a broad name search alone is sufficient only when the destination is already uniquely identified and locally verified.
reasoning.content: Resolve and open the start first, then constrain destination searches with the city, neighborhood, or nearby address; treat the Search Results list as text matches—not a nearest-place ranking—and open each plausible result to verify its full displayed name, address, category, and qualifying attributes, including every tie or near-identical variant. Compare plausible candidates by using “Find directions between two points,” entering the verified start and destination, selecting the walking profile, and running the route; report the closest verified candidate only after reading the complete route panel, including every visible turn, total distance, and estimated time rather than inferring them from the map.

reasoning.title: Anchor, verify, then calculate the walking route
reasoning.description: Use for map tasks asking for the nearest place meeting specific ownership, chain, category, or locality criteria; do not treat broad search results or visual proximity as proof of qualification or shortest walking distance.
reasoning.content: Resolve and open the full starting address first, then search within that vicinity, open each plausible place’s detail view to verify its complete name, address, category, and required attributes, and compare close candidates—including ties—using “Find directions between two points” with the walking profile. Avoid unanchored searches whose results may be statewide text matches rather than nearest locations; once routed, report the full visible destination, total distance, estimated time, and every displayed turn-by-turn step without guessing or omitting near-identical qualifying variants.
